absent: Locking and lifetime rules for dump control, tap list and NFS handle use are not shown.
Implementation and contracts of the core dump starter and stage callbacks are not shown.
Numeric sizes for verifier, stateid parts, session identifier and device identifier are not shown.
Numeric values of the NFSv4 errors tested by the sequence check are not shown.
Export markings, boot phase mapping and wire encodings beyond listed constants are not shown.

findings.text: Dump control groups three stage operations for start dump and done plus an extended ack pointer, an opaque caller context pointer, an owner module pointer, a minimum allocation size and a flags word.
Dump start ensures the control owner defaults to the current module when unset and then delegates to the core dump starter with socket, message, header and control, returning its result.
Tap registration groups a network device pointer with an owner module pointer and a list node so taps can be chained.
NFS_LOCALIO_PROGRAM is 400122, LOCALIOPROC_NULL is 0 and LOCALIOPROC_UUID_IS_LOCAL is 1.
NFS_MAXFHSIZE is 128.
File handle pairs a short length with a fixed byte store sized by the maximum, where only the leading length bytes are meaningful.
Handle comparison reports difference when lengths differ or when leading bytes differ over the first length. Handle copy propagates source length and leading bytes to the target.
NFS_UNSTABLE is 0, NFS_DATA_SYNC is 1, NFS_FILE_SYNC is 2 and NFS_INVALID_STABLE_HOW is minus 1 as an internal invalid marker.
Handle hash feeds the leading handle bytes defined by the stored length into a little endian CRC with all ones seed and inverts the result.
NFS3_POST_OP_ATTR_WORDS is 22.
Header inclusion markers _LINUX_NFS_H, _LINUX_NFS3_H and _LINUX_NFS4_H guard the NFS, NFSv3 and NFSv4 headers.

Access entry carries numeric type, flag and mask plus a who discriminator for named, owner, group or everyone, with a union holding either a user or group identity. Access list carries a count followed by a trailing variable length entry array.
Security label carries file system, policy and identifier numbers plus a length and a pointer to label bytes. NFS4_MAXLABELLEN is 2048.

State identifier offers two views of shared storage, either opaque bytes or a packed sequence number plus other bytes, with a classifier for invalid, special, open, lock, delegation, layout, data server, revoked and freed variants. Verifier is a fixed opaque byte container.

Operation numbers start at OP_ACCESS at 3 and run through file, namespace and locking operations into session, layout, copy, seek and clone extensions ending at OP_REMOVEXATTR at 75, with OP_ILLEGAL at 10044. Base ends at release lockowner, 4.1 at reclaim complete and 4.2 at remove xattr.
FIRST_NFS4_OP equals OP_ACCESS, LAST_NFS40_OP equals OP_RELEASE_LOCKOWNER, LAST_NFS41_OP equals OP_RECLAIM_COMPLETE, LAST_NFS42_OP equals OP_REMOVEXATTR and LAST_NFS4_OP aliases LAST_NFS42_OP.
NFS4ERR_RESET_TO_MDS is 12001, NFS4ERR_RESET_TO_PNFS is 12002 and NFS4ERR_FATAL_IOERROR is 12003.

Sequence mutating check returns false for NFS4ERR_STALE_CLIENTID, NFS4ERR_STALE_STATEID, NFS4ERR_BAD_STATEID, NFS4ERR_BAD_SEQID, NFS4ERR_BADXDR, NFS4ERR_RESOURCE, NFS4ERR_NOFILEHANDLE and NFS4ERR_MOVED, and true for all other codes.
NF4BAD is 0, NF4REG is 1, NF4DIR is 2, NF4BLK is 3, NF4CHR is 4, NF4LNK is 5, NF4SOCK is 6, NF4FIFO is 7, NF4ATTRDIR is 8 and NF4NAMEDATTR is 9.

Open claim values are NULL 0, PREVIOUS 1, DELEGATE_CUR 2, DELEGATE_PREV 3, FH 4, DELEG_CUR_FH 5 and DELEG_PREV_FH 6. Open types are NOCREATE 0 and CREATE 1. Create modes are UNCHECKED 0, GUARDED 1, EXCLUSIVE 2 and EXCLUSIVE4_1 3. Limits are SIZE 1 and BLOCKS 2.

Delegation values are NONE 0, READ 1, WRITE 2, NONE_EXT 3, READ_ATTRS_DELEG 4 and WRITE_ATTRS_DELEG 5. No delegation reasons are NOT_WANTED 0, CONTENTION 1, RESOURCE 2, NOT_SUPP_FTYPE 3, WRITE_DELEG_NOT_SUPP_FTYPE 4, NOT_SUPP_UPGRADE 5, NOT_SUPP_DOWNGRADE 6, CANCELLED 7 and IS_DIR 8. Lock types are UNLOCK 0, READ 1, WRITE 2, READW 3 and WRITEW 4.

Base attributes run 0 to 55 from FATTR4_SUPPORTED_ATTRS to FATTR4_MOUNTED_ON_FILEID. Extensions run 56 to 76 from FATTR4_DIR_NOTIF_DELAY to FATTR4_FS_CHARSET_CAP, then 77 to 80 from FATTR4_CLONE_BLKSIZE to FATTR4_SEC_LABEL, plus FATTR4_MODE_UMASK at 81, FATTR4_XATTR_SUPPORT at 82 and FATTR4_UNCACHEABLE_FILE_DATA at 87.

Attribute mask uses three words where word zero holds attributes 0 to 31 directly, word one holds 32 to 63 shifted down by 32 and word two holds 64 and above shifted down by 64, each mask bit selecting one attribute.

THRESHOLD_RD, THRESHOLD_WR, THRESHOLD_RD_IO and THRESHOLD_WR_IO are single bit flags for positions 0 to 3. NFSPROC4_NULL is 0 and NFSPROC4_COMPOUND is 1. NFS4_VERSION is 4 and NFS4_MINOR_VERSION is 0. NFS4_DEBUG is 1.

Client operation identifiers start at NFSPROC4_CLNT_NULL and increase through I/O, open, attribute, lease, lock, namespace and security helpers into session, layout and device helpers and then allocation, clone, copy and xattr helpers, ending at NFSPROC4_CLNT_OFFLOAD_STATUS.
Session identifier is a fixed opaque byte array sized by the maximum session length.
SESSION4_PERSIST is 1, SESSION4_BACK_CHAN is 2, SESSION4_RDMA is 4 and SESSION4_FLAG_MASK_A is 7. SP4_NONE is 0, SP4_MACH_CRED is 1 and SP4_SSV is 2.
GDD4_OK is 0 and GDD4_UNAVAIL is 1. Layout types are NFSV4_1_FILES 1, OSD2_OBJECTS 2, BLOCK_VOLUME 3, FLEX_FILES 4 and SCSI 5 with a following max sentinel.
RETURN_FILE is 1, RETURN_FSID is 2 and RETURN_ALL is 3. IOMODE_READ is 1, IOMODE_RW is 2 and IOMODE_ANY is 3. NOTIFY_DEVICEID4_CHANGE is 2 and NOTIFY_DEVICEID4_DELETE is 4.
Block volumes are SIMPLE 0, SLICE 1, CONCAT 2, STRIPE 3 and SCSI 4. Block extent states are READWRITE 0, READ 1, INVALID 2 and NONE 3.
Block extent wire size equals seven network order words plus one device identifier. SCSI range wire size equals four network order words.
Code sets are BINARY 1, ASCII 2 and UTF8 3. Designators are T10 1, EUI64 2, NAA 3 and NAME 8.
NFL4_UFLG_MASK is 0x0000003F, NFL4_UFLG_DENSE is 1, NFL4_UFLG_COMMIT_THRU_MDS is 2 and NFL4_UFLG_STRIPE_UNIT_SIZE_MASK is 0xFFFFFFC0.
Comparison, copy and hash follow the stored handle length without visible bound enforcement, so callers must keep length within the maximum and avoid overlapping storage surprises.
